decisions.statement: A property's values are written into the files `page-entry-writing` names.
A file that is not there is made rather than refused.
A file already with the text that would be written is left alone.
Every file the disk changed at is named in the answer.
A file left alone is named nowhere in the answer.
A file numbered past the last file written is taken away.
An appended value rolls into the next numbered file where the ceiling is reached.
The bytes already in a file count toward the ceiling.
A file already past the ceiling stays past it under an append and is divided only by a landing.
A line handed over already formed is written as handed rather than made again.
A file's fill is read from that file's size rather than from that file's text.
A property held uncommitted is written into files whose names say so.
A value rolls into a file named as the file that value rolled out of is named.
Writing beside a page that is not there is refused.
A refusal names the page or the file the refusal is about.
The values written here are read back by `page-entries` in the order written.
Nothing here makes a directory.
Nothing here mints an id.
Nothing here judges a value against the shape declaring that value.
Nothing here reads the index.
A caller wanting the files written here claimed files them itself.
Nothing here commits.
Nothing here has a lock against another writer of the same file.
Landing a property's values whole is this module's test fixtures rather than code.
That landing is the oracle an appending writer's rolling is proved against.

definition: a page's entry values put on the disk beside that page
